prior_importants.description: The 'nested package missing a script' debt passes on its kind alone, with no figure and no `sameFiles`. So once that debt is accepted for a package, a commit past the pin can add any number of new files there and the remeasure lands them. No test or typecheck measured those files, and no ledger entry names them.
After a re-gate, the remeasure holds a flag to the first gate's figures. The ledger never records the larger figure the re-gate accepted, so a merge no worse than the re-gated pin refuses.

findings.description: The critical-area check compares only tree(pin) with tree(head). It does not compare what the merge commit landed with what merging the pin there would have landed. A head on an older base can bring back a critical-area change that the target reverted after the pin, and no --approved-by is asked for.
findings.body:
**A head on an older base can undo a critical-area revert on the target without `--approved-by`.**

[`remeasureMerge`](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/eb5adcc1bb5e62457862d8a7d7b2fa10de709cc0/src/core/land-remeasure.service.ts#L86-L105) asks for `--approved-by` only when `git diff <sha> <head>` lists a path under `CRITICAL_PATHS`. That diff shows how the head's tree differs from the pin's. What actually lands is GitHub's three-way merge of `head` onto `landedOn`, whose base is `merge-base(head, landedOn)`, not the pin's merge-base.

`--remeasure` drops the descends-from-pin check ([land.service.ts L242](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/eb5adcc1bb5e62457862d8a7d7b2fa10de709cc0/src/core/land.service.ts#L242-L248)), so the head can sit on an older base than the pin. When it does, the two diffs disagree.

**Trigger** (the session's scope-in covers critical file X, so the scope audit passes):
1. The target at `T1` holds X=V1. The gate pins `sha`, which descends from `T1`, so X=V1 there.
2. The target later reverts X to V0, the content at an older ancestor `B0`. `landedOn` has X=V0.
3. The session force-pushes `head`, a commit on `B0` that keeps X=V1. A human merges it on GitHub. With base V0, ours V0 and theirs V1, the result is V1.
4. `pup land <s> --remeasure`: `git diff sha head` does not show X, so no approval is asked for. `mergedOnto` matches, because the tree is exactly merge-tree(landedOn, head). The stages pass, and the land goes through.

Landing the pin itself would have kept the revert, because its merge-base is at or after `T1`. Here a critical-area change that the target reverted lands again, unapproved. Nothing else in `measureBranch` treats critical paths specially.

[ADR 0185 L98-L101](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/eb5adcc1bb5e62457862d8a7d7b2fa10de709cc0/docs/adr/0185-pup-land-remeasure-takes-a-moved-head-on-the.md#L91-L106) justifies the tree diff only for the opposite case: an older-base head that keeps a change the pin had reverted. Neither *What it does not catch* nor *Not caught* lists this case.

**Possible fix:** also diff what landed beyond the pin's own landing. In the scratch git dir, as `mergedOnto` does, compute `pinTree = git merge-tree --write-tree --no-messages <landedOn> <sha>`. Then diff `<pinTree> <mergeCommit>^{tree}` with the same safe flags and `--name-only -z`, and take the union of its critical paths with the `<sha> <head>` list. If merging the pin there conflicts, fail closed and require `--approved-by`.

process_issues.description: Round 4 importants-only budget: skipped conventions, docs, simplicity, context, maintainability; spec skipped (no closing issue or spec source); workflow-safety skipped (no .github/workflows change).
Consolidator not spawned: only one finding came back from the reviewers, so there was nothing to group; dedup was done inline.

Prior important prior_importants[2] (re-gate figures not recorded in the ledger) is still unresolved at eb5adcc: `accepted` is still built only from `measured.openEntries` (land-remeasure.service.ts:185-192).
One security instance had `git show` of commit 52a5005 refused, so it checked the nested-package sameFiles fix from the current file instead.
